exposure: Recumbent labor positioning with a low-dose epidural
Upright labor positioning with a low-dose epidural
outcome: Cesarean deliveries in the first pregnancy
Cesarean deliveries in the second pregnancy
Uterine ruptures in the second pregnancy
Maternal deaths in the first delivery
Maternal deaths in the second delivery
cohort: A theoretical cohort of 756,000 nulliparous individuals in the United States who have a term birth annually and receive an epidural.
finding: Laboring in the recumbent position with a low-dose epidural was projected to save $157 million annually and improve maternal outcomes, including fewer cesarean deliveries and maternal deaths, compared to the upright position.
mod_finding: Recumbent positioning with a low-dose epidural was associated with 18,652 fewer cesarean deliveries in the first pregnancy and 11,228 fewer cesarean deliveries in the second pregnancy compared to the upright position.
